fixes.red_test: AppLifecycleGuardTest.FR_APP_026_sharedRouterDoesNotRetainDroppedApps: AssertionError 'never-started apps still reachable through the shared Router expected:<0> but was:<30>'
fixes.rationale_full: Router.mounts held a strong Mount -> RegistrationLog -> owner app chain, so every app that ever mounted a shared Router stayed reachable (never-started forever, shut-down until a later Router registration). Mount now holds its RegistrationLog through a WeakReference (the app keeps its log strongly, so a live app's mount never clears); owners() prunes cleared and terminated mounts, and admitRouterLocked skips a mount cleared after owners() ran (its app is gone, so nothing watches or records there). Monitor order and the owners() contract are unchanged. Test: 30 never-started and 10 started+shut-down apps mount one Router and are dropped; polling System.gc() with a 10 s deadline, all 40 are collected without any later registration, and a live app still mounts and receives registrations. Mutation check: an extra strong field on Mount turned the test red again (30 reachable); restored -> green.

fixes.red_test: ProtectOnlyTest.SEC_AUTH_006_AC3_registrationRacingOnStartIsRefused: ComparisonFailure 'a Pattern registration during auth's onStart escaped protectOnly expected:<re[fus]ed> but was:<re[gister]ed>'
fixes.rationale_full: Under protectOnly, an unjudgeable (Pattern/array) registration made after the doctor read the unjudgeable list but before started=true (e.g. while seed() runs) was neither a doctor FAIL nor refused, so it was served unauthenticated. A rangeClosed flag is set, holding the unjudgeable list's lock, as the first step of auth's onStart; watchRange checks rangeClosed||started and appends under the same lock, so a registration either lands in the list before the doctor reads it (start FAIL) or throws IllegalStateException (not applied, not served). Test blocks the .user seed inside onStart with a latch, registers app.get(Pattern) from the main thread, releases: the registration must throw and /raced is not served. Mutation check: commenting out 'rangeClosed = true' turned it red again; restored -> green.

fixes.red_test: WebSocketWrapperTest.FR_FLOW_008_AC6_wrappedRegistrationsAreCounted: AssertionError 'an unwrapped /raw route was not reported'
fixes.rationale_full: The doctor compared the WEBSOCKET registration count with the number of auth.webSocket() calls, so an unregistered wrapper hid an unwrapped route (false negative) and one wrapper on two routes warned (false positive). auth.webSocket(handler) now returns a private WrappedWebSocket (same behaviour as the former lambda: track the principal/expiry, then call the handler); webSocketItems counts WEBSOCKET registrations whose getTarget() is this auth's WrappedWebSocket and WARNs when routes > wrapped, keeping the existing message format ('N WebSocket routes but M use of auth.webSocket(handler); ...'). The unused private counter webSocketWrappers was removed. Public signature of webSocket() unchanged (returns WebSocketHandler). Docs (ko+en) now say the doctor counts wrapped registrations. Mutation check: restoring call counting turned the test red again; restored -> green. Existing AC-6 tests (2 routes / 1 use) still green.

fixes.red_test: AuthStoreDefaultsTest.IR_FLOW_003_AC2_sharedFileThrottleReadsTheLatestAuthsClock: AssertionError 'the shared throttle still reads the first Auth's frozen clock expected:<0> but was:<60000>'
fixes.rationale_full: The per-FileUserStore shared FileLoginThrottle/FileDeviceTrust were built with the first builder's TimeSource and Logger forever. A new static FILE_TARGETS map (WeakHashMap keyed by the FileUserStore, like the store maps) holds a SharedTargets per FileUserStore: a re-pointable SwitchedTime (TimeSource) and a ComponentLogger. The shared refresh store, throttle and device trust are now constructed over those targets, and every successful build() that uses a shared default re-points them to that Auth's .timeSource and ComponentLogger (only after all validations pass); install(app) re-points them again. Result: the shared defaults follow the Auth most recently built or installed over that FileUserStore. Mutation check: disabling both repoint calls turned the test red again; restored -> green. Docs (ko+en) state the rule.

fixes.red_test: RefreshTokenStoreTest.FR_TOKEN_002_AC5_interruptDuringStopStillStopsTheCleanupThread: AssertionError '[... ERROR onStop callback failed null] expected:<0> but was:<1>'
fixes.rationale_full: An interrupt pending on the stopping thread made hashSlots/background.awaitTermination throw InterruptedException, so onStop failed before stopCleanup(): the cleanup executor kept running and the final throttle/device snapshot was lost. onStop now catches InterruptedException around the awaits (one WARN), always runs stopCleanup(), and restores the interrupt flag at the end. stopCleanup() itself now runs the final snapshotRun even when its own awaitTermination is interrupted, then rethrows. Test: W8 app, 3 logins, interrupt the test thread, shutdown: no 'onStop callback failed', app TERMINATED, and the cleanup thread terminates (polled with a 10 s deadline). Mutation check: rethrowing the InterruptedException in onStop turned it red again; restored -> green.

fixes.red_test: AuthStoreDefaultsTest.REL_FLOW_001_sharedFileDefaultsLogToTheLatestApp: AssertionError '[...app B log lines...] expected:<1> but was:<0>' (the cap WARN went to the stopped app A's logger)
fixes.rationale_full: Same root cause and fix as M2-F19: the shared file defaults (refresh store, login throttle, device trust) now log through the per-FileUserStore SharedTargets ComponentLogger, which build() and install() re-point to the latest Auth's ComponentLogger (itself forwarding to that app's logger when no .logger is set). Test: app A (logger LA) + Auth a installed, started, stopped; app B (logger LB) + Auth b over the same FileUserStore installed and started; 100,002 distinct keys through b.loginThrottle() -> exactly one cap WARN in LB, none new in LA. Mutation check: disabling the repoint calls turned it red again; restored -> green.

fixes.red_test: FileSecretsTest.FR_IAM_015_AC3_decoratedFileUserStoreIsHeldToTheKeyRule: AssertionError 'PROD built over a decorated FileUserStore without a key'
fixes.rationale_full: The PROD file-key rule, the DEV WARN, the doctor 'plain secret values in auth files' count and the file-state checks only recognised a bare FileUserStore, so ForwardingUserStore(FileUserStore) (the documented decorator base) built in PROD and wrote plain hashes. ForwardingUserStore's constructor now records its delegate in a new internal registry utils.auth.internal.UserStoreDelegates (weak keys, weak values; same bridge pattern as FileStoreKeys, since delegate() is protected in another package). Auth.fileUserStoreIn(UserStore) unwraps the decorator chain (bounded depth 64) and is used by unkeyedFileStores(), plainSecretItems() and fileStateItems(). The file-default store selection (refresh/throttle/device trust beside the users file) is deliberately unchanged: still only for a bare FileUserStore (documented). Test: one and two decorator layers over an unkeyed FileUserStore fail PROD build() naming 'new FileUserStore(file, AuthFileKey)', the file and NARU_AUTH_FILE_KEY; a keyed decorated store builds; in DEV the doctor counts the decorated store's plain hash ('1 ...'). Mutation check: making fileUserStoreIn stop unwrapping turned it red again; restored -> green.

fixes.red_test: FileSecretsTest.SEC_IAM_008_AC5_undeletableBackupAfterMigrationOnlyWarns: AuthConfigException 'key file ... failed to provide a signing key (IOException: cannot delete the replaced raw key .../.naru-auth.key.bak; delete it by hand)'
fixes.rationale_full: User decision residual->fix. On a file system whose rename does not replace (Windows), a failed delete of the raw .bak after a successful enc(...) migration threw IOException and failed build(), leaving the raw key beside the encrypted one. Added a package-private seam KeySources.FileKey.Moves (rename/delete; REAL = File.renameTo/delete) plus FileKey.moves(Moves) for tests; replaceWith uses it. A failed final delete now logs one WARN naming only the file paths (never key bytes) and returns, so the migrated key is used. On the next read of a key file that opens as enc(...), a leftover .bak is deleted under the creation locks (only while the key file exists, so the createOnce crash-restore path is untouched); a failed delete there is one WARN. The WARN goes to auth's logger: Auth.keySet now calls the package-private FileKey.signingKey(Logger) (same key result as KeySource.keys() for FileKey, which has no kid); the public signingKey() logs to a ConsoleLogger. POSIX test simulates a non-replacing rename and an undeletable .bak through the seam: PROD build succeeds with the migrated key, key file sealed, exactly one WARN naming the .bak, no line holds the raw key (ISO-8859-1, base64url or base64), then a normal read deletes the .bak. Mutation checks: restoring the throw -> red (AuthConfigException); disabling the next-read cleanup -> red ('the next read deletes the leftover raw .bak'); restored -> green. Docs (ko+en) migration bullet updated.

public_api_changes: none: no public symbol added, removed or re-signed. Internal/package-private only: new internal class utils.auth.internal.UserStoreDelegates (FileStoreKeys-style bridge, outside the API contract); ForwardingUserStore constructor records its delegate (behaviour otherwise unchanged); package-private KeySources.FileKey.Moves seam, FileKey.moves(Moves), FileKey.signingKey(Logger); package-private Auth.SharedTargets, Auth.SwitchedTime, Auth.fileUserStoreIn; private Auth.WrappedWebSocket (auth.webSocket still returns WebSocketHandler); private counter Auth.webSocketWrappers removed; RegistrationLog.Mount.log is now a weak reference read through log().
docs_changed: docs/api/auth.md (auth.webSocket doctor counting; shared file defaults follow the latest built/installed Auth's clock and logger; decorated FileUserStore held to the key rule; Windows key-migration .bak WARN + next-read cleanup)
